A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OmniEdit research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite relocated displays and revised training-data counts.

before.justification: v1 reports original automatic and human evaluations on Omni-Edit-Bench, importance-sampling and architecture ablations, and appendix comparisons against specialist models.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Table 3 and Appendix Tables 5–7, together with qualitative editing comparisons.

M1.justification: The seven-specialist framework, GPT-4o-to-InternVL2 distillation, score-threshold weighting, EditNet architecture, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Details shortened in the main specialist descriptions remain in Appendix A.1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training sources, seven editing tasks, and aspect-ratio coverage. Evaluation still uses 62 images and 434 edits from the same benchmark. Revised training sample counts do not establish additional coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same eight baselines and human-evaluation comparators. The architectural controls and three specialist comparisons also remain unchanged. Newly cited BrushNet and Paint by Inpaint are not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported training set changes from 775,000 to 1,220,000 examples, substantially altering task proportions: background swaps increase from 50,000 to 180,000, and removal and addition each increase from 100,000 to 200,000. The unfiltered ablation budget changes from 775K to 1.2M. These are substantial reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish reruns. Epoch count, benchmark, metrics, and human-evaluation procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing importance-sampling ablation is revised to use 1.2M unfiltered examples instead of 775K, while retaining its question and reported scores. Architecture ablations, specialist comparisons, and qualitative case studies retain their evidence; moving their displays to the appendix does not add analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The four-rater human-evaluation description is unchanged.

E6.justification: The main, ablation, and specialist performance tables retain identical values after matching renumbered tables. OmniEdit's GPT-4o overall score remains 6.98, Gemini overall score 5.78, and human accuracy 0.55. Qualitative examples and preliminary skill ratings also match. Training-count revisions do not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the ground-truth distribution assumption, KL-divergence derivation, importance-weighting definition, and learning objective are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical correction appears.

C1.justification: The abstract's four contributions and claims of broad editing capability and superiority remain unchanged, as does the concluding contribution statement. The introduction drops a numerical performance summary, but the underlying superiority claim and supporting results remain.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations concerning specialist supervision, text-representation updates, intermediate interactions, and preservation of generation capabilities. The limitation imposed by SD3 and proposed future use of stronger base models are unchanged.

D1.justification: The training-data breakdown is revised, and the pre-filtering total is corrected from 52,000,000 to 5,200,000, matching the unchanged component counts. Existing generation instructions, scoring prompts, model configuration, hardware, and resource-access statement remain. v2's prose still gives 150K object-swap examples despite its table reporting 180K.

R1.justification: Section 6 and the bibliography add Paint by Inpaint by Wasserman et al. and BrushNet by Ju et al. These are limited background citation additions; the substantive positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 trims the introduction's performance summary and several specialist descriptions, expands the pipeline caption, and updates publication, contact, and contribution text. Most prose and the section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The evidence displays are substantially reorganized: both ablation tables and both architectural case-study figures move from the main text to the appendix. Figures 1 and 5 are reduced, the abstract begins on page 1 and continues onto page 2, and other floats are repositioned. Existing visual evidence is retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the pipeline explanation, adds two relevant citations, and corrects the pre-filtering total. However, the substantially revised training counts accompany identical results without explaining their relationship, and a new 150K-versus-180K object-swap inconsistency appears. These reporting ambiguities prevent a reliable net quality judgment; the larger stated dataset alone does not demonstrate improvement.
